ImageDescription.value:
7 Khasiat Buah Pisang Yang Tak Pernah Di Duga 
     Pisang merupakan salah satu buah yang di gemari oleh semua lapisan masyarakat dari berbagai usia. Ini dikarenakan, buah ini mudah di dapatkan di semua tempat serta dengan harga yang relatif terjangkau. Buah ini sangat cocok sebagai makanan pencuci mulut setelah makan. Maka dari itulah, banyak di antara kita yang menghidangkan buah ini di menu hariannya. Mengkonsumsi pisang ternyata banyak sekali manfaatnya bagi kesehatan tubuh. Ada berbagai khasiat buah pisang yang tak pernah anda duga sebelumnya. Lalu apa saja khasiat buah pisang bagi kesehatan tubuh tersebut...???



    Sahabat, tips kesehatan. Seperti aneka buah-buahan lainnya, buah pisang juga memiliki khasiat atau manfaat saat di konsumsi. Banyak di antara kita yang memercayai bahwa buah ini memiliki berbagai khasiat tersembunyi didalamnya. Maka dari itulah, untuk memperjelas berbagai khasiat buah pisang, tips kesehatan akan mengungkapkan berbagai khasiat buah yang satu ini. Berikut ini khasiat buah pisang yang tak pernah anda duga :

   Menurunkan berat badan secara alami. Bagi anda yang bermasalah dengan berat badan, maka rutin mengkonsumsi buah ini dapat membantu menurunkan berat badan yang anda miliki. Ini dikarenakan, buah ini mengandung jumlah kalori yang relatif kecil.
   Menyeimbangkan jumlah cairan dalam tubuh. Tubuh membutuhkan jumlah cairan yang cukup untuk menunjang semua kinerja organ dalam tubuh. Oleh karena itulah, kandungan kalium pada pisang sangat penting untuk membantu menyeimbangkan jumlah cairan dalam tubuh tersebut.
   Mudah terserang penyakit seperti flu, batuk dan lain-lainnya...???. Mulailah makan buah pisang. Kandungan vitamin C pada buah ini membantu meningkatkan sistem kekebalan tubuh yang anda miliki.
   Ingin tulang yang sehat...???. Mengkonsumsi buah pisang secara rutin dapat membantu menyehatkan tulang anda. Ini dikarenakan, buah ini merupakan salah satu buah yang mengandung mangan yang cukup tinggi.
   Meningkatkan energi yang dibutuhkan tubuh secara instan. Saat aktivitas harian meningkat, konsumsilah buah pisang. Ini bertujuan agar tubuh tidak cepat capek maupun lelah di padatnya aktivitas atau pekerjaan anda.
   Memperlancar sistem pencernaan pada tubuh anda. Mengkonsumsi buah ini secara rutin dapat membantu kinerja sistem pencernaan anda lebih baik lagi. Sehingga berbagai nutrisi dari makanan yang anda konsumsi dapat di serap dan digunakan oleh tubuh secara optimal pula.
   Sebagai obat sembelit yang alami. Buah pisang dapat membantu memperlancar buang air besar anda. Maka dari itulah, konsumsilah buah pisang untuk menghindari mengerasnya feces sebagai gejala awal sembelit.

ImageDescription.value:
Kylemore Gardens, Co Galway is the location of this photo. It is part of the Kylemore House / Abbey estate. The Gardens were built along with Kylemore House between 1867 and 1871.

It Transpires that there were 21 heated glass houses including a 60 foot banana house, vineries, peachery, ferneries and exotic fruit and veg of all kinds.

Tropical fruit such as bananas oranges and pineapples along with grapes peaches and other items were raised in the heated greenhouses, which I think is very impressive for a house in Connemara over 140 years ago.

ImageDescription.value: A camera-less photographic work by Amanda Means, created by shining the light from a darkroom enlarger directly through the water glass. The enlarger light passes through the water and glass to create varying levels of opacity and translucency, projected onto a sheet of photo paper. This method reveals a rich and detailed landscape beyond the familiarity of the everyday object. Bubbles, scratches, and condensation become enlarged, intensified; a mysterious world unto their own. Traditional silver gelatin print.

ImageDescription.value:
An open domestic refrigerator with food and drink at night.
The photo is stacked for focus and light from five photos.
The only light source used is the normal lamp in the fridge.
The fridge in an Electrolux, model ERB34253W with a net volume of 188 litres (6.6 cu ft).
The fridge contains four eggs, a green bell pepper, a jar of chili, three bottles of grapefruit soda, three cans of coconut milk, three bottles of pear cider, a bottle of carbonated water, a bottle of soy sauce, a plate of sliced ham, a container with butter, a round cheese, a jar of sliced, pickled cucumber, a pitcher with crushed, roasted cacao beans, two lemons, some tomatoes, a box with grapes, carrots, yellow onions and oranges. The fridge is in Brastad, Lysekil Municipality, Sweden.

ImageDescription.value:
An orange—specifically, the sweet orange—is the citrus Citrus × ?sinensis (Citrus Sinensis (L.) Osbeck) and its fruit. It is the most commonly grown tree fruit in the world.

The orange is a hybrid of ancient cultivated origin, possibly between pomelo (Citrus maxima) and mandarin (Citrus reticulata). It is an evergreen flowering tree generally growing to 9–10 m in height (although very old speciments have reached 15 m). The leaves are arranged alternately, are ovate in shape with crenulate margins and are 4–10 cm long. The orange fruit is a hesperidium, a type of berry.

Orange trees are widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical climates for the delicious sweet fruit, which is peeled or cut (to avoid the bitter rind) and eaten whole, or processed to extract orange juice, and also for the fragrant peel. In 2008, 68.5 million tons of oranges were grown worldwide, primarily in Brazil and the State of Florida in the US.

Oranges probably originated in Southeast Asia and were cultivated in China by 2500 BC. The fruit of Citrus sinensis is called sweet orange to distinguish it from Citrus aurantium, the bitter orange. The name is thought to ultimately derive from the Sanskrit[10] for the orange tree, with its final form developing after passing through numerous intermediate languages.

I found this orchard on Fairmont Dr. and checked it out. They seem to have peach, orange and avocado trees, and a large bee hive operation back away from the street.

These coils of heavy wire are used when they plant a new tree. The coil of fencing is put around the new seedling to keep the critters from eating the new plants.

I know I have too many pictures of oranges, but that is one thing that sets apart our town of Redlands, CA from many others. And, having grown up in the Midwest, I never had an idea that oranges grew on trees. I just saw them in grocery stores, once a year. They were such a treat that parents used to give them to the children for a Christmas present.

ImageDescription.value: This grove in Prospect Park is owned by the CIty of Redlands.  Though the city, like others in California, is hurting for money, it seems they are not interested in selling the fruit from this grove. The oranges are left to ripen and fall to the ground. It makes a statement about two things: Abundance and Waste.

ImageDescription.value:
(1 in a multiple picture set)
If you can drive only one street in Redlands, CA, you should drive east on Highland Ave., starting at Cajon Street. You will see all kinds of homes, none new. Their are stately mansions, and simpler cottages like this one. But they all blend just fine. This is the sort of street that brings Hollywood producers to our town. They can find just about any background scene they are looking for.

ImageDescription.value:
Woerner Orchardsâ Bradley Woerner donates unsold fruits and produce to D.C. Central Kitchens at the close of the USDA Farmers Market, which celebrates the close of its 22nd season on Oct 27, 2017, in Washington, DC. The last market day featured live music from the U.S. Army Band, farm animal exhibits. Visitors were able to bowl with squash, help harvest and learn about sweet potatoes for DC Central Kitchen, pick and paint pumpkins, meet farm animals, shop for fresh picked local produce from the Chesapeake Bay Region, enjoy prepared foods, see live turkeys from Tall Cotton Farm, get a farm animal and veggie-themed temporary tattoo to wear, and shop for food inspired art work. âVegUâ Program Coordinators prepared and talk about a pumpkin curry soup recipe during free 10-minute fruit and vegetable classes at the âVegU(cation)â tent where people learned how to how to pick, store, and prepare pumpkin curry soup. Fruits and vegetables are featured during their peak harvest time. The USDA farmers market is located on the corner of 12th Street and Independence Ave, SW; features live music, 30+ farmers, ranchers, and small business owners in the Chesapeake Bay Region. The festival played host to thousands of visitors from around America and looks to open May 4, 2018. For more information visit usda.gov/farmersmarket or follow @USDA_AMS on Twitter and Instagram using hashtag #USDAFarmersMkt. View photos of the market on Flickr. USDA Photo by Lance Cheung.

PUMPKIN CURRY SOUP Yields 8 cups Prep Time: 1 hour | Cook Time: 20 minutes | Total Time: 1 hour 20 minutes 1 tbsp. olive oil 1 medium onion, ï¬nely chopped 3 garlic cloves, minced 3 lb. fresh sugar pumpkin 3 cups vegetable stock 1 tbsp. curry powder 1 tsp. chili powder Salt and pepper to taste

1. Preheat oven to 350Â° F. 2. Remove pumpkin stem and slice pumpkin in half using a sharp knife. Remove pumpkin seeds and stringy innards with a spoon. Discard or save seeds to roast later on. 3. Brush pumpkin halves with oil and place face down on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake for 45 minutes or until tender. 4. Remove from oven and let cool. Separate pumpkin ï¬esh from skin. PurÃ©e the pumpkin ï¬esh in a blender or food processor. (Process to your preference of a smooth to chunky texture. See photo album for examples.) 5. In a pot, heat onion and garlic over medium heat. Add vegetable stock, purÃ©ed pumpkin, curry powder and chili powder. 6. Bring soup to a boil then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes. Note: Each pound of sugar pumpkin should yield 1 cup of pumpkin purÃ©e.

THIS WEEK VEGU IS ALL ABOUT PUMPKINS

Three diï¬erent species in the Curburita genus are known as pumpkins (Cucurbita pepo, C. maxima, C. moschata). Pumpkins are typically planted in early summer and harvested in fall. Pumpkins can be stored for several months after harvesting due to their thick outer skin. There are countless diï¬erent varieties of pumpkins grown in the United States ranging in size from 2 pounds to 100 pounds and in an array of colors including orange, yellow, green, and white. One of the most common pumpkin varieties used for cooking and baking is Sugar Pie (also known as pie pumpkins), which has thin skin and sweet ï¬esh making it ideal for eating. HOW TO PICK Look at size. Choose pumpkins that feel solid and heavy for their size. Check for blemishes. Pick pumpkins that are unblemished, have consistent color and have the stems attached. Feel for freshness. Press on the bottom of the pumpkin. If it is ï¬exible or has several soft spots it may indicate that it is not as fresh. HOW TO PREPARE To cook a fresh pumpkin, ï¬rst wash and dry the whole pumpkin. Remove the stem and slice the pumpkin in half using a sharp knife. Clean out the inside, removing the seeds and ï¬brous strings. Place the halves on a cookie sheet or tray and bake at 350Âº F for about 30-45 minutes depending on the size. Once cooled, peel oï¬ the skin using a knife and chop the pumpkin into cubes, or purÃ©e the ï¬esh in a blender or food processor. Use cooked pumpkin purÃ©e or cubes in pies, cakes, baked goods, soups, and stews. HOW TO STORE Pumpkins require cool and dry conditions for best storage. Optimal temperature is between 50-55Âº F and humidity of 50-70%. If stored properly, certain varieties of pumpkin can last up to two months. Tip: Store cooked, cubed or purÃ©ed pumpkin for up to one week in the refrigerator. Advice about freezing. Freezing pumpkin is a great option. To freeze, ï¬rst roast pumpkin in the oven (as outlined on the other side of this handout) and place cooked cubes or purÃ©ed pumpkin into freezer bags. To freeze raw cubes, ï¬rst peel the pumpkin skin and remove seeds and ï¬brous strings. Chop pumpkin into 1-inch cubes and store loosely in freezer bags. Frozen pumpkin can be stored for 9 months to 1 year. FUN FACTS â¢Pumpkins originated in Central America and are botanically a fruit. â¢At the ï¬rst Thanksgiving feast in 1621, the pilgrims did not serve pumpkin pie, rather, they served stewed pumpkin. â¢Pumpkins are members of the Cucurbitaceae family, which includes squash, zucchini, watermelon, cucumbers and gourds. â¢Over 50,000 acres of pumpkins were harvested in the United States in 2014, producing 1.3 billion pounds of pumpkins. â¢China and India are the worldâs top pumpkin producers; U.S. is ranked ï¬fth. â¢Illinois is the top pumpkin producing state in the U.S. followed by California, Ohio and Pennsylvania. â¢Pumpkin is an excellent source of beta-carotene, the precursor to vitamin A.

ImageDescription.value: ​民國50年代，當兵抽到「金馬獎」的父親，趁著難得的返臺假期，帶著軍中袍澤到桃園市復興區的家中體驗農村生活，好友兩人站在三合院古厝前，身上披著使用山棕製成的棕蓑，一起與從家中果樹摘下來的滿籃新鮮海梨柑與年柑合照，照片中的父親，一如往常地展現他淳樸靦腆的笑容。今日，父親早已白髮蒼蒼，已不是當年的那位年輕小伙子，但在父親身上，不變的是那股農家子弟知足喜樂的精神!

a. Molecular structure of MdMYB1-1 and MdMYB1-2 alleles with flanking sequences. The insertion sites upstream of MdMYB1-1 and MdMYB1-2 are indicated by a red line (HFTH1) and golden yellow line (GDDH13), respectively. 
b. Images of 12 well-known apple varieties with non-red or red skin colour (upper panel) and PCR-based screen showing the absence (right) or presence (left) of the LTR retrotransposon insertion in the upstream of MdMYB1. A 750 bp fragment corresponding to the partial of redTE that is absent in non-red-skinned varieties (lanes 1 to 6) and is present only in red-skinned varieties (lanes 7 to 12). Lane 13, control check (purified water was used as the template), Lane 14, positive control.

Artist.value: Carl Henry Moen

ImageDescription.value:
The photographer's father and brother are shown on the porch of the family's home in Ballard. Younger sister Agnes is seen peeking through the window.

Carl Henry Moen was born in Seattle in 1892 to Norwegian immigrant parents. His family moved several times as he was growing up, but settled in Ballard when he was nine years old. He helped harvest and sell the produce, milk, and poultry his family raised, and also was a messenger for Western Union, dug clams, and worked for Bemis Bag Co. Eventually he left home and began a 30-year career as a sailor, crossing the Pacific Ocean over 200 times. Moen bought his first camera in 1909; it was a 5x7 view camera that used glass plate negatives. A bedroom closet in the Moen house served as his darkroom. Most of his photos from this period are of his family and friends, showing scenes of life in Ballard in the early part of the 20th century.

title: File:History Bites- Russell Powell - New England Apples.webm
current_title: File:History Bites- Russell Powell - New England Apples.webm

ObjectName.value: History Bites- Russell Powell - New England Apples

Categories.value: Apples|Media from YouTube|WebM videos|License review needed (video)|Uploaded with video2commons|Video display resolution 1920 x 1080|Videos in American English

ImageDescription.value:
“As American as apple pie…” Apples have been part of American history and folklore since colonial days. Orchards used to cover the hillsides of New England until Prohibition times when most of the trees, which were used more for the production of hard cider than edible fruit, were cut down. But now that cider is coming back into fashion, the orchards with their many varieties of new and heirloom apples are being

regrown.

This fascinating lecture will offer advice about rare heirlooms and newly discovered varieties, comments on the rich tradition of apple growing in New England and on the “fathers” of American apples―Massachusetts natives John Chapman (“Johnny Appleseed”) and Henry David Thoreau. Apples of New England will present the apple in all its splendor: as biological wonder, super food, work of art, and cultural icon.

Russell Steven Powell served as executive director of the New England Apple Association from 1998 to 2011, and since then has been its senior writer. He publishes the blog newenglandorchards.org, and is the author of America’s Apple. He was founding editor and publisher of New England Watershed Magazine, named Best New Publication of 2006 by Utne Reader. Powell produced and directed the award-winning video documentary Shack Time (2001), about the artists’ shacks in the dunes of the Cape Cod National Seashore, and his paintings have been exhibited in New York City

and Cape Cod. He lives in Hatfield, Massachusetts.

current_title: File:Strawberry Pippin apples, along with oranges and apples.jpg

ObjectName.value: Strawberry Pippin apples, along with oranges and apples

Categories.value: Apples|CC-Zero|Self-published work

ImageDescription.value:
Strawberry Pippin apples

Strawberry Pippin apples are a medium-sized variety, and tend toward round or slightly flat and have some ribbing. They are known as particularly beautiful apples, with a tough, light yellow skin layered with red striping. The side facing the sun is often blushed red or pink. Strawberry Pippin apples can potentially be grown in the Philippines, but their success depends largely on the growing conditions. Apples generally thrive in temperate climates with distinct seasons and cooler temperatures. In the Philippines, they are more likely to perform well in high-altitude areas such as Benguet, Bukidnon, or Mt. Apo, where the cooler temperatures mimic the chill hours required for proper flowering and fruiting. These regions provide a suitable environment for certain apple varieties to thrive. One important factor to consider is the chill hour requirement of Strawberry Pippin apples. This variety may need a specific amount of cold exposure (below 7°C or 45°F) to break dormancy and set fruit. While the Philippines is better suited for low-chill or tropical apple varieties, careful experimentation and attention to cultivation practices may allow Strawberry Pippins to adapt. Proper soil conditions, including well-drained loamy soil with a pH between 6.0 and 7.0, are essential for their growth. Additionally, consistent watering is needed, especially during dry months, but overwatering should be avoided to prevent root rot. As a self-sterile variety, Strawberry Pippin apples require a compatible pollinator variety planted nearby for successful fruiting. Selecting an appropriate pollinator that flowers at the same time is critical. In the tropical climate of the Philippines, pest and disease management is also a challenge, as the warm weather may encourage issues not typically seen in temperate zones. Regular monitoring and control measures, whether organic or chemical, can help address these problems.

Farmers and enthusiasts in the Philippines have successfully grown non-native fruits like apples through grafting techniques and selecting rootstocks suited to local conditions. If you saw Strawberry Pippin apples in Cebu markets, they were likely imported or grown in cooler highland areas. To grow them successfully, it’s advisable to source saplings from a reliable nursery and consult local agricultural experts. If cultivating Strawberry Pippin proves difficult, exploring similar tropical apple varieties might be a practical alternative.

artist_raw: Mona Sokol

Categories.value: Apples|Self-published work

ImageDescription.value: Po dawnych ogrodach bojkowskich pozostały dzikie drzewa owocowe,które stanowią cenne świadectwo tradycyjnej uprawy w Bieszczadach. Wiele z tych drzew, szczególnie jabłonie, grusze, wiśnie czy śliwy, mogą mieć dziko rosnące formy, które przez lata wykształciły swoją odporność na lokalne warunki klimatyczne i glebowe. Te drzewa mają szczególną wartość nie tylko historyczną, ale także ekologiczną, przyciągając dzikie zwierzęta i owady. W Bieszczadach często zachowały się także tzw. ogrody leśne, w których współistniały rośliny dzikie i uprawiane. Te obszary są niezwykle interesujące pod względem ekologicznym i kulturowym.

title: File:Chuối mốc.jpg
artist_raw: Lê Huỳnh Bộ

Categories.value: Vietnam|Bananas|Self-published work|Uploaded with Mobile/Android|Photographs taken on 2025-05-25

ImageDescription.value:
đây là chuối mốc, một giống chuối.

Chuối (danh pháp khoa học: Musa spp.) là một loại cây thân thảo lâu năm thuộc họ Musaceae, có nguồn gốc từ khu vực nhiệt đới Đông Nam Á. Trái chuối là một loại quả giả hình dạng thuôn dài, mọc thành nải, có vỏ ngoài màu xanh khi non và chuyển sang màu vàng khi chín. Chuối là nguồn cung cấp năng lượng dồi dào nhờ hàm lượng carbohydrate cao, đặc biệt là đường tự nhiên như fructose, glucose và sucrose. Bên cạnh đó, chuối chứa nhiều vitamin (như vitamin C, B6) và khoáng chất (đặc biệt là kali), đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc duy trì huyết áp ổn định và chức năng tim mạch. Nhờ giá trị dinh dưỡng cao, chuối không chỉ là loại trái cây phổ biến trong khẩu phần ăn hàng ngày mà còn được nghiên cứu và ứng dụng trong các lĩnh vực y học, dinh dưỡng và công nghệ thực phẩm.

Hình tôi chụp tại Hòa Tiến, Hòa Vang, Đà Nẵng, Việt Nam.

ImageDescription.value:
🍏 A Apfelwiese Dilldorfer é um pequeno pomar encantador que aparece no caminho antes de alcançar a ponte próxima à antiga Ruhrlandkaserne, em Dilldorfer Höhe. Com suas macieiras espalhadas e frutos amadurecendo ao sol, esse trecho oferece uma pausa natural e tranquila no percurso — quase como um portal verde entre o passado militar da região e o presente residencial e ecológico.
🌳 A localização estratégica da Apfelwiese, entre trilhas como o Baldeneysteig e áreas de proteção ambiental, reforça o charme do lugar. É um ponto onde a natureza se manifesta com simplicidade, mas também com significado: um símbolo de renovação e vida em uma área que já foi marcada por estruturas rígidas e cercas militares.

ImageDescription.value: The bag of apples was full of "liquid". At the bottom of the bag, there was "one bad apple". The apple was in the active phase of decay also called "liquefying rot stage".  The “liquefying rot stage” is one of the strangest phases of fruit decomposition. Pectin gets broken apart. Cell walls collapse.  The tissue stops holding its shape. The inside liquefies first. The skin forms a little shell. The fruit collapses inward.
